transcript: So I have not seen Stereophonic on tour yet. I have seen it on Broadway, I've seen it off Broadway, I've seen it in the West End. And it's really interesting to me how many people are going to the tour and absolutely hating it and saying, you know, the same criticisms that we heard in the past iterations of it's too long, it's boring, yada, yada, yada. And I get it, it is. It is a show that is not for everyone. I know it's very hyped because it does what it wants to do incredibly well, but it's very long and it's tedious, and that's the point. And so if you're not into that, if you don't. If you don't attach yourselves to these characters right away, it's not gonna be a pleasant experience and it's just. It's not gonna be for you. Right. But what I find really interesting is the people that take the fact that they didn't enjoy it and turn that around into the writing is bad and that it's too long and it needs to be cut down. Because the writing being long and a little tedious is the point. It's the point of the show. There's also a lot of really fascinating aspects of the show, like the toxic relationships and toxic behaviour that we accept in the name of art. And I think, in a way, that the length of the show also feeds into that. But a big part of Stereophonic as a Show is how much blood, sweat and tears goes into creating a piece of art. But also the mundane moments are part of creating a piece of art. And spoilers for Act 2, but especially if you left at intermission. This all really, to me, comes together in the final moments of the show, when they're having this meeting, talking about all of the songs that they've cut from the album and how the album still isn't down to the size that they need it. And you realise in that scene that all of the songs that you've seen them painstakingly put together in the show have been cut from the album. Everything that we saw them do is no longer a part of the final product. And yet, without it, we wouldn't have had that final product of this album that they released that we never get to hear anything from. And yet, despite cutting all of that, they still need to cut more in order to do a single album because of the The time constraints of a vinyl record. Right. They have to cut down four more minutes, and what do they cut from that? And I think the same thought process can be said about any piece of art, about how there's many pieces of art that could arguably be better by cutting certain aspects. This play being one of them. You know, it. It could definitely be shorter, but all of the craftsmanship that went Into creating those scenes. How do you cut that? What do you cut? And, you know, what is all of the work behind those pieces that are left on the cutting room floor of any piece of collaborative art. Right? Anyway, Stereophonic is a brilliant play, and it's. It's not for everyone, but to say that it's bad writing is just incorrect. It's incorrect. It just may. It just may not be for you.
